answer: Require each agent to post a refundable bond before earning fees, and slash it when random audits expose duplicate identities or fabricated work. A Sybil attacker must lock capital for every persona and risks losing each bond, so multiplying identities becomes costly rather than free. Honest agents recover their bonds, while the oasis of cheap shells fades; as rewards grow on the horizon, bonds can rise accordingly. This raises the cost of attack without claiming a perfect zenith of trust.
